notes.title: Korean pastimes
notes.text: Baseball (야구) is Korea's most-watched sport, with cheering songs for every player. Hiking (등산) is hugely popular with older Koreans — you'll see them in full colorful gear on every mountain trail.

notes.title: 노래방
notes.text: 노래방 ("song room") are private karaoke rooms rented by the hour, open late at night. Friends, coworkers and families all go. Scores appear on screen after every song.

notes.title: Webtoons
notes.text: Webtoons (웹툰) are Korean comics made for phones, read by scrolling down. Many hit K-dramas started as webtoons, such as Yumi's Cells and Itaewon Class. You can read many for free on apps like Naver Webtoon.

notes.title: 오랜만이에요
notes.text: When you meet someone after a long time, say 오랜만이에요 ("it's been a long time"). It's one of the most common greetings in Korean — and in K-dramas, it often comes right before a dramatic reunion.

notes.title: 좋아해요 vs 사랑해요
notes.text: 좋아해요 means "I like you" — the classic K-drama confession. 사랑해요 ("I love you") is much heavier and usually comes later. A confession is called 고백.
